paper_sections.title: Neural representations of relevant and irrelevant features in perceptual decision making.
Main effects of task and stimulus type
Attention and accumulation in the frontal and parietal lobes

description.value: The study examined how attending to motion versus color alters BOLD representations of relevant and irrelevant stimulus features during perceptual decisions, using modeling and connectivity analyses to distinguish attentional from accumulation-related regions.

design.value: Five highly trained subjects performed a fully crossed motion/color coherence discrimination task during six functional MRI task sessions. Across runs, subjects attended either to motion direction or to predominant color while ignoring the other feature; motion and color coherence varied independently. Separate motion and color localizer tasks and independent training-session MRI data were used to define regions of interest.

source_definition.value: Six levels of motion coherence, including a 0% coherence control; individually calibrated coherence values were used to target 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, and 100% performance.
Motion coherence used to parameterize attend-color trials, in which motion was the ignored feature.
Six levels of color coherence, including a 0% coherence control; individually calibrated coherence values were used to target 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, and 100% performance.
Color coherence used to parameterize attend-motion trials, in which color was the ignored feature.
The attended feature was either the overall direction of motion or the predominant color of the dot stimulus.
The feature other than the one relevant to the task during a given run.

description.value: Five subjects, ages 26–38; two males, all right-handed, with normal or corrected-to-normal vision and normal neuroanatomy reviewed by a neurologist.

inclusion_criteria.value: normal neuroanatomy as reviewed by a neurologist

task_description.value: Subjects performed a visual dot motion or color proportion task on a stimulus consisting of multiple colored moving dots. One feature, motion or color, was relevant to the task during a given run while the other feature was ignored. Motion and color coherence varied independently in a fully crossed factorial design.

instructions.value: For each attend-motion trial, subjects were required to identify the direction of motion as quickly and accurately as possible. For each attend-color trial, subjects were required to identify the predominant color as quickly and accurately as possible. Each run began with a colored text prompt directing the subject to perform either the motion or color task for all trials within the run.

stimuli.value: Multiple colored moving dots within a central circular aperture of 7.5° diameter. A subset of dots moved coherently leftward or rightward on a background of randomly moving dots, and an uncorrelated subset of dots of one color, blue or red, was present on a background of evenly apportioned blue and red dots. The stimulus appeared for 2500 ms; dot density was fixed at 16.7 dots · deg−2 · s−1 and dot velocity at 5 deg/s.

task_description.value: Subjects viewed 10 repetitions of a 40 s trial in which the motion stimulus was present for 10 s, followed by 30 s of a static dot display. The motion stimulus consisted of 10 consecutive 1 s presentations of 100% dot motion coherence with directions chosen randomly, without replacement, from [0, 36, 72, … 324°].

design_type.value: 10 repetitions of a 40 s trial with 10 s stimulus and 30 s static display

stimuli.value: 100% dot motion coherence with randomly chosen directions, followed by a static dot display

task_description.value: The color localizer task consisted of 10 repetitions of a 40 s trial. The 10 s color stimulus consisted of 10 consecutive 1 s stationary displays in which colored squares were shown, followed by a 30 s interval in which the same type of stimulus was shown in grayscale.

design_type.value: 10 repetitions of a 40 s trial with 10 s stimulus and 30 s grayscale display

stimuli.value: Stationary colored squares subtending 0.57° at a density of 16.7 squares/deg2; 24 fully saturated colors were selected from xyY space, including the blue and red hues used in the main experiment.

instrument.value: Siemens MAGNETOM Trio 3T MR Scanner at the Henry H. Wheeler, Jr., Brain Imaging Center at the University of California, Berkeley

description.value: Functional images consisted of 24 slices acquired with a gradient echoplanar imaging protocol.
Anatomical images consisted of 160 slices acquired using a T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid-acquisition gradient echo protocol.

instrument.value: ASL Eye-Trac 6 LRO; ViewPoint Eye Tracker (Close-Focus Camera and Illuminator)

description.value: Eye movement data for three subjects was acquired at the Neuroimaging Center at the University of California, San Francisco, Medical Center using an ASL Eye-Trac 6 LRO. Data for the other two subjects was collected during training sessions at the University of California, Berkeley, using a ViewPoint Eye Tracker.

reason_no_modality_class_used.value: Eye tracking is not MRI, EEG, fNIRS, or PET.

description.value: Functional images were converted to 4D NIfTI format, corrected for slice-timing offsets, motion corrected, smoothed, coregistered to structural images, and normalized to a standard MNI_N27 volume.

steps.value: Functional images were converted to 4D NIfTI format.
Images were corrected for slice-timing offsets.
Motion correction was performed using AFNI 3dvolreg, with the reference volume set to the mean image of the first run.
Images were smoothed with a 5 mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel.
Coregistration was performed with AFNI 3dAllineate using the local Pearson correlation cost function for fMRI-to-MRI structural alignment.
The inverse transformation was used to warp the anatomical image to functional image space.
Anatomical images were normalized using FSL fnirt to the MNI_N27 standard volume.
The same normalization parameters were applied to native-space statistical maps as necessary for group statistical maps.

model_settings.value: The model consisted of A′ bearing on the decision threshold, k describing the relationship between motion coherence and mean drift rate, and TR representing fixed residual processing time in seconds. It fit reaction time and accuracy data simultaneously.

estimator.value: An iterative procedure designed to optimize the log-likelihood (Lp) of the diffusion model fit

hrf_model.value: γ probability density function peaking at 6 s

model_settings.value: Separate regressors modeled six levels of motion coherence, six levels of color coherence, and the attended/ignored feature. Linear trend contrasts used the relevant coherence vector transformed to zero mean with a sum of squares equal to 1.

model_type.value: fixed-effects summary statistic with an overlap requirement

model_settings.value: The voxelwise t statistic was divided by the square root of the number of subjects (n = 5), compared against a standard normal null distribution at p = 0.001 for the full group, with at least three of five subjects required to show a significant single-subject effect at p < 0.05.

hrf_model.value: piecewise b-spline basis functions separated by 2 s intervals for 20 s after onset

model_settings.value: The model estimated the hemodynamic response for each combination of feature and coherence within each ROI.

model_type.value: random-effects t test and repeated-measures ANOVA

model_settings.value: ROI-extracted data were submitted to random-effects t tests or repeated-measures ANOVA.

estimator.value: random-effects t test or repeated-measures ANOVA

model_type.value: multiplicative bottom-up and top-down attention model

model_settings.value: The model represented the MT+ BOLD response as bottom-up input modulated multiplicatively by an attentional factor. The attentional factor differed from baseline for the duration of the reaction time and returned to baseline thereafter; bottom-up input persisted for the full 2500 ms stimulus presentation. The model used 25 inputs and eight parameters.

After detrending, fMRI time courses were averaged across voxels within V4, MT+, middle intraparietal sulcus, and inferior frontal sulcus ROIs. Granger causality values were computed for each run in segments of 35 TRs and initially segregated by attentional condition; conditional Granger causality was also computed.

estimator.value: multivariate autoregressive prediction of upcoming time points

description.value: Subjects identified leftward or rightward motion as quickly and accurately as possible while ignoring the color feature.
Subjects identified the predominant red or blue color as quickly and accurately as possible while ignoring the motion feature.
The motion stimulus was present for 10 s and consisted of 10 consecutive 1 s presentations of 100% dot motion coherence.
A static dot display was presented for 30 s after the motion stimulus.
Stationary colored-square displays were presented for 10 s, consisting of 10 consecutive 1 s displays.
The same type of stimulus was shown in grayscale during the 30 s interval between color displays.

definition.value: Negative linear parametric variation of the BOLD response with attended motion coherence, corresponding to greater activity for harder than easier motion conditions.

multiple_comparison_method.value: fixed-effects summary statistic with an overlap requirement

interpretations.value: The BOLD response decreases with increasing motion coherence when motion is attended.

definition.value: Negative linear parametric variation of the BOLD response with attended color coherence, corresponding to greater activity for harder than easier color conditions.

multiple_comparison_method.value: fixed-effects summary statistic with an overlap requirement

interpretations.value: The BOLD response decreases with increasing color coherence when color is attended.
